I've learned that it's all about finding that balance. It's not about being perfect; it's about making the most of every day and taking care of myself. I've had my ups and downs over the years, but I've come to realize that it's the little things that count. Whether it's a short walk around the block or a quiet moment of meditation, it's all about taking care of my body and mind. And when the weather gets tough, I find ways to stay active indoors or make the most of the good days. It's a journey, not a destination, and I'm just trying to enjoy the ride.

I've also learned the importance of maintaining a good diet. Since I have Type 2 Diabetes, I have to be careful with my carb intake. I used to love pasta and bread, but now I've learned to swap them out for healthier options—whole grains, lean proteins, and lots of veggies. It was hard at first, but now it's just second nature. My go-to breakfast is usually Greek yogurt with nuts and berries or eggs with avocado. Lunch is something simple, like grilled chicken and a salad. And dinner? I love making soups, especially in the winter—there's nothing better than a warm bowl of homemade vegetable soup when it's freezing outside!

It's funny how much of a difference small changes can make. I used to get so tired after meals, but now I feel more energized than ever. Of course, it's not just about what I eat, but also how I eat. I try to slow down and enjoy my meals, savoring each bite. It's amazing how much of a difference that makes in how I feel.

I'm not going to lie, there are still days when I struggle. Some days, I just want to indulge in my favorite comfort foods, but I know that's not good for me. So, I remind myself of why I'm doing this and how far I've come. It's all about balance, and it's okay to indulge every now and then. The key is to find that balance and make choices that work for me.

Exercise has been a bit of a journey for me. I used to think you had to go all out—like running miles or lifting heavy weights—but I've found that consistency is more important than intensity. Walking has been my best friend; it's low impact, which is great for my osteoarthritis, and it helps with my blood sugar levels. I also try to do some light yoga a few times a week. I never thought I'd be someone who did yoga, but it actually helps a lot with my joint pain and flexibility. On days when the weather's bad, I use a stationary bike or do some at-home workouts. Nothing fancy, just enough to keep me moving.

Sleep has been another area where I've had to make changes. I used to stay up late watching TV, but now I have a bedtime routine that helps me wind down. I avoid caffeine after 3 PM, keep my bedroom cool and dark, and read a book before bed instead of looking at my phone. It's made a huge difference. I feel more rested and refreshed in the morning, and it's helped with my blood pressure and joint pain. It's funny how something as simple as sleep can have such a big impact on our overall health.

Stress management has also been a game-changer for me. Stress is a huge trigger for my hypertension, and when life gets busy, I can feel it physically. I've started practicing mindfulness—just five minutes of deep breathing or meditation in the morning. It sounded silly to me at first, but it actually works. I also keep a gratitude journal where I jot down three good things that happened each day. It helps me stay positive, even on tough days. It's amazing how much of a difference these small habits can make in managing stress and keeping me healthy.

Hydration has also become a priority for me. I used to not drink enough water when I was younger, but now I make a conscious effort to stay hydrated. It helps with my energy levels, digestion, and even my skin. I keep a big water bottle with me all day, and I try to drink herbal teas in the evening instead of coffee. Kansas summers can be brutal, so I make sure to drink even more water when it's hot outside.

I also make sure to stay on top of preventative care. I get my regular check-ups, take my medications on time, and get my vaccines every year—flu shot, pneumonia shot, and now the new RSV vaccine. I also make sure to get my annual mammogram and keep an eye on my bone density, since osteoporosis runs in my family. I figure that the best way to stay healthy is to catch problems early before they become bigger issues.

The biggest challenge for me is motivation. Some days, I just don't feel like working out or cooking a healthy meal. I used to be really hard on myself about that, but now I've learned to give myself grace. If I have an off day, I just try to make better choices the next day. It's not about being perfect, it's about being consistent.

Overall, I'm feeling pretty good about where I am. I know I can't control everything about my health, but I do what I can to stay strong and feel my best. If I've learned anything over the years, it's that small habits add up. It's not about drastic changes—it's about making choices every day that support my well-being. I'm in it for the long haul!
